# Questions for Dana Okafor — 2025 Schedule C / SE prep

These are the points the documents genuinely leave open. Each shows the effect on the
return, using figures from `schedule_c.json`. Answer by line number in your reply.

**Q1 — Do the Beacon ($9,200) and Orchard ($12,200) 1099-NEC totals represent payments
that reached you through PayHub?** Your PayHub 1099-K gross ($41,350 for 61
transactions) is the only source of those clients' income in the bank data — there are
no separate Beacon or Orchard deposits. If any part of those NEC totals was paid to
you outside PayHub (check, another account, cash), Schedule C line 1 must increase by
that amount — all income you actually received must be reported. Right now I report
line 1 = $41,350 (PayHub gross) + $9,400 (Tessaro direct ACH) = $50,750, and I assume
Beacon's $9,200 and Orchard's $12,200 are already inside the $41,350. The Tessaro 1099-NEC
($18,500) vs. the $9,400 of direct deposits is the same issue: was the $9,100
difference routed through PayHub?

**Q2 — Was the June 13 Denver flight (Southwest $389.00) personal?** The bank shows
Denver spending that month for REI, House of Blues, the Denver Palace Hotel, and a
"VENMO: DENVER TRIP SPLIT" between personal contacts, so I classified the flight as
personal. If it was a business trip, tell me the business purpose and it moves to
travel (line 24a, +$389.00).

**Q3 — Were any of your March meals business-related?** I claimed only the two San
Francisco meals on the confirmed October client trip ($64.00 + $126.00, 50% limit →
line 24b = $95.00). The four March Austin debits — Picklor ($52.00, 3rd), Bar Bar
Blackboard ($132.00, 17th), Life is Beautiful Fest ($78.00, 21st), Hardy's ($74.00,
22nd) — are personal absent a business purpose. Your email says "meals are business,"
but Pub. 463 (library) requires substantiation. Each documented business meal adds 50%
of its cost to line 24b; all four business → line 24b rises to $95.00 + $168.00 =
$263.00.

**Q4 — Was the MacBook Pro 14 ($2,149.00, charged to your personal Apple Care on
2025-09-14) used 100% for business?** You wrote it became your main work machine, so I
expensed it (de minimis, under $2,500). If you also used it personally, tell me the
business percentage — line 27a falls by 2,149.00 × (personal %). Also: your email says
"that July MacBook" but the charge date is September 14 — if there was a *second*
Apple purchase in July I need the receipt.

**Q5 — What percentage of your phone ($1,020/yr T-Mobile) and internet ($840/yr
Spectrum) use is business?** You did not give a percentage. I applied **80% as an
assumption** (line 25 = $1,488.00). The library's Schedule C instructions require a
documented business-use percentage. At 100% line 25 = $1,860.00; at 50% = $930.00; at
0% = $0.

**Q6 — Where is page 2 of the mileage notebook, and are the 1,150 "misc client
errands" miles 2025 business miles?** Page 1 references it; it was not photographed.
It supports 1,150 of the 1,428 miles I deducted ($805.00 of line 9). Also, the header
(4,860 total, 1,200 Larkspur commute) and the itemized trips don't fully tie — please
confirm 4,860 is your 2025 total and that the 1,200 Larkspur figure is the commute.

**Q7 — Do you regularly use part of your home as your principal place of business?**
If yes, Pub. 463 can make the 2,232 miles driving between home and the Capital Factory
coworking space deductible business travel rather than commuting, which would increase
line 9 by up to 2,232 × $0.70 = $1,562.40. If no, those miles stay nondeductible
commuting.

**Q8 — Larkspur payroll reconciliation.** Your W-2 box 1 is $24,800 and withholding was
$4,207.20 (fed $2,310.00, SS $1,537.60, Medicare $359.60), implying $20,592.80
take-home, but only $19,502.80 of Larkspur deposits hit this account — a $1,090.00
difference. Any final check stub, payout to another account, or deduction to explain
it? (This affects the Form 1040 wage side only, not Schedule C.)

**Q9 — Missing insurance premiums: where were they paid?** Two gaps in this account:
(a) BCBS shows eight $380.00 premiums (May–Dec) but you said $380/month all year —
were January–April ($1,520) paid from another account or employer withholding? Only
premiums you actually paid can go on Schedule 1 line 17. (b) Hiscox billed quarterly
(Jan/Apr/Jul $160.00) — was the expected Oct 20 installment paid elsewhere or not paid
at all? If paid from another account, line 15 (and Schedule 1) increase.

facts.answer: Oh — yes, the ~1,200 miles Jan–April were me driving to the Larkspur office every day. I guess that's commuting? The rest is client stuff and the coworking space.
PayHub takes 2.9% off the top before paying out. The 1099-K number is before their cut.
Phone and internet are maybe 60% work? I don't have a separate line.
Denver was my cousin's wedding, nothing work-related.
Beacon and Orchard both pay me through PayHub. Tessaro pays by bank transfer.
That's my own health plan after I left Larkspur. Not through any employer.
